import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns

# Load the dataset
df = pd.read_csv('data/cameras.csv')

# Set a style for the plot
sns.set_style("whitegrid")

# Create the figure and axes
plt.figure(figsize=(12, 8))

# Create a scatter plot showing the relationship between megapixels and price,
# with sensor type distinguished by color.
# Using a log scale for price_usd as it often has a wide, skewed distribution.
sns.scatterplot(
    data=df,
    x='megapixels',
    y='price_usd',
    hue='sensor_type',
    palette='viridis',
    s=100,  # size of the markers
    alpha=0.7, # transparency
    edgecolor='w', # white edge for markers
    linewidth=0.5 # line width for marker edge
)

# Set the y-axis to a logarithmic scale for better distribution visibility
plt.yscale('log')

# Add title and labels
plt.title('Camera Price vs. Megapixels by Sensor Type', fontsize=16)
plt.xlabel('Megapixels', fontsize=12)
plt.ylabel('Price (USD, Log Scale)', fontsize=12)

# Improve the legend placement
plt.legend(title='Sensor Type', bbox_to_anchor=(1.05, 1), loc='upper left')

# Adjust layout to prevent labels from overlapping
plt.tight_layout()

# Save the figure
plt.savefig('output.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=150)
